title: Support email triage
tagline: Sorts each customer email by topic and urgency, looks up the order, and drafts a reply for a person to check.
what_it_does: An online homeware shop gets a steady stream of customer emails: late parcels, refunds, broken items, questions. This Python script reads each new email and asks Claude to sort it into one of five topics with an urgency from 1 to 3. Anything that sounds like a safety problem is always treated as most urgent.

The script then finds the order number, looks up the order, and asks Claude to draft a reply that follows the shop's policy and tone. Urgent emails and high-value orders are flagged for a manager. A person on the support team reviews each draft before it goes out.
built_with: Python (standard library only), the Anthropic API, a CSV order table
diagram_caption: Blue steps are automated. The dashed orange step is done by a person.

cases.label: Safety: a spark from the base

input.Subject: Sparks from the base
input.Email: Hello, my kettle (order EX-300101) gave off a small spark from the base when I switched it on this morning. I have unplugged it. Is it safe?
input.Order lookup (the project's code): Order EX-300101: Stainless steel kettle, status delivered, shipped 2026-05-02, value GBP 58.00

cases.prompt:
SYSTEM
Sort each customer email for an online homeware store.
Choose exactly one topic: refund, late_parcel, damaged_item, product_question, other.
Urgency: 1 = routine, 2 = customer is waiting on us, 3 = angry, repeated contact, safety issue or legal threat.
Any mention of scalding, sparks, burning smell or a cracked element is urgency 3 whatever the tone.
Reply with JSON only: {"topic": "...", "urgency": 1, "reason": "one short sentence"}

USER
Subject: Sparks from the base

Hello, my kettle (order EX-300101) gave off a small spark from the base when I switched it on this morning. I have unplugged it. Is it safe?
cases.prompt_note: This is the first of the project's two prompts, the one that sorts the email, filled in by the project's own code. Only the opening line was changed, to remove the shop's name. The second prompt drafts the reply using the shop's private refund, delivery and safety policy, so it is not shown. 'Flagged for a manager' is the project's own rule, applied to the sorting result and the order.
cases.output:
Step 1, sorting: topic damaged_item, urgency 3. A spark from the base is a safety issue.
Flagged for a manager: yes

Step 2, draft reply for a person to check:

Hi Ines,

Thank you for unplugging the kettle straight away. Please do not use it again. A manager will call you within one working day to arrange a replacement or a refund, whichever you prefer, and to collect the faulty kettle at no cost to you.

Kind regards,
The support team
